body:
Can't reproduce with 0.1.6 on Sierra:

```
$ nvim -u NORC /tmp/newfile
1000i9<esc>
y0
:<c-r>"<cr>
```

@akashin

Could you retry with the latest release 0.1.6? Homebrew seems to be up-to-date as well.
In debug mode we have an assert that catches too big numbers (`> INTMAX_MAX`) in `getdigits_safe()` (older versions catch this in `getdigits()`). That is what @akashin triggers.
Except this was a `RelWithDebInfo` build.  That shouldn't have the debug asserts, should it?

Oh, we do enable assertions for that.

```
108 # Enable assertions for RelWithDebInfo.
109 if(CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO MATCHES DNDEBUG)
110   string(REPLACE "-DNDEBUG" "" CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO "${CMAKE_C_FLAGS_RELWITHDEBINFO}")
111 endif()
```

Oh. I blame the [Homebrew formula](https://github.com/neovim/homebrew-neovim/blob/master/Formula/neovim.rb#L131-L136).

You have to `brew install neovim --with-release` to get the `Release`. IMHO, it should be opt-out instead. Something like `brew install neovim --with-debug-info` to get `RelWithDebInfo`.

We decided awhile ago that we want assertions and symbols by default, even for end-users. RelWithDebInfo supposedly doesn't have a performance cost (except size).

>  In debug mode we have an assert that catches too big numbers (> INTMAX_MAX) in getdigits_safe() (older versions catch this in getdigits())

Where is the assert in `getdigits_safe()` ? 

This bug is present on 0.1.6, so whatever is calling `getdigits()` should be changed to call `getdigits_safe()`. It doesn't make sense to assert on user input.

It's not in getdigits_safe.  It's in getdigits, which is what getdigits_long is calling for the `:[range]` uses.

There are a lot of places in Vim which expect numbers to get clamped to the range of the data type, which we're now violating with this assert.  I'm not that this specific assert is worthwhile.

I noticed that we have some other functions which have a `_strict` variant.  If we think there are valid places to use the getdigits family of functions with the asserts, then how about exposing those through `getdigits*_strict` instead?

@jamessan Sounds good to me. I wasn't real happy with the `_safe` idiom. (And I agree this needs to be more opt-in than opt-out, unless someone does the work of making sure user input isn't reaching these functions)

issue.title: Crash in ex mode

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
Just something I came across when fuzzing Neovim. Should this be fixed? It's not likely ever to be accidentally stumbled upon.. It's caused by a failing assertion in `getdigits()` in `charset.c`.

### Actual behaviour
Neovim crashses

### Expected behaviour
Neovim produces an error message

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`
```
nvim -u NORC
Q9999999999999999999<enter>
```
